introduction: On this Sunday, Abraham welcomes three mysterious visitors at Mamre with generous hospitality, and they promise him a son. In the Gospel, Jesus visits Martha and Mary; Martha is busy serving while Mary sits at his feet listening, and Jesus says that Mary has chosen the better part. Paul speaks of Christ in us, the hope of glory. Let us welcome the Lord and listen to him.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord comes to visit us. Let us welcome him and bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may combine generous service with attentive listening to the Lord. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who serve others in their homes, in hospitals and in parishes: that they may not be worn out but find rest in Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who welcome strangers and guests: that they may recognize the Lord in those they receive. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are anxious and troubled about many things: that they may find peace at the feet of Jesus. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may choose the better part and make time each day to listen to the Lord. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, you visit us in our guests and in your word. Give us the generosity of Abraham and the attentiveness of Mary, so that we may welcome your Son. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: The better part
reflection.body:
It is the hottest part of the day, and Abraham is sitting at the entrance of his tent. Three strangers appear. Abraham runs to meet them, bows down, and begs them to stay: "please don't go away from your servant." He hurries to Sarah to bake bread, chooses a tender calf, and serves them himself. His hospitality is generous and joyful. And in welcoming strangers, Abraham welcomes the Lord, who promises: "Sarah your wife will have a son."

In the Gospel, Jesus is welcomed into the home of Martha and her sister Mary. Martha throws herself into the work of hospitality. Mary "sat at Jesus' feet and heard his word." Martha becomes frustrated and complains to Jesus: "Lord, don't you care that my sister left me to serve alone? Ask her therefore to help me."

Jesus answers gently, repeating her name: "Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things, but one thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good part, which will not be taken away from her."

Jesus is not criticizing service. Abraham's service in the first reading is praised. What troubles Martha is not her work but her anxiety, and the way it pulls her away from the guest she is serving. Jesus invites her, and us, to put first things first: to listen to him. Service flows best from that.

Paul speaks of the mystery hidden for ages and now revealed: "Christ in you, the hope of glory." The Lord is not only a guest who visits us; he wants to live in us.

Many of us are more like Martha than Mary. This week, make room for the better part: a few minutes each day sitting at the Lord's feet, listening to his word, without rushing. And when you serve, serve with peace, not anxiety.
